读者来信

工部局选举
“无礼”的反思

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，我既不是天之骄子，也不是在工部局选举中独立利益的英勇捍卫者。我打算投票，而且既然我相信民主的保障代表权的方法，我将根据那些我已授权代表我行事的人向我提出的“候选人名单”进行投票。请允许我冒昧发表一些相当无礼的看法吗？我注意到，人们大肆渲染工部局令人震惊的缄默。我也注意到——作为一名勤奋的新闻读者——恐怕在过去三年里，贵报的专栏几乎充斥着关于工部局事务的大量资料，甚至到了拥挤不堪的地步。如果你问我是否想知道工部局与其他机构就越界筑路等主题进行的谈判的每一个细微细节，我会说是的：这是基于那位女士对告知她自己在秘密部门工作的男士所发出的命令的原则——“告诉我一些秘密”。然而，我确实意识到，如果将这些轻率的举动透露给新闻界，就不会有谈判，也不可能有达成协议的希望。我还听说工部局需要“新鲜血液”和“新人”。那么利德尔先生（据我所知他很成功）和基勒里先生怎么样呢？后者的履历显示，他已经赢得了世界上最重要的英国公司之一的信任，如果他成为工部局成员，肯定会对上海有用，仅仅因为他显然能接触到英国本土的真正领袖人物，这就是一笔不可忽视的资产？我还听到很多关于“缺乏领导力”、需要“不怕采取行动的人”的议论。好吧，这里已经展现了领导力，并以明确的决心采取了行动，而现在我们却听到软弱的叫喊，反对被强迫、被发号施令或侵犯天生蠢货的神圣权利。先生，请允许我温和地评论一句：这是什么胡言乱语，什么废话连篇？问问任何工会会员，当给他一张“候选人名单”时，他是否认为自己在被发号施令。当然不会。这张名单是由他任命来制作该文件的人给他的。正如您所指出的，三个英国组织的执行委员会就是我们要委托制作这份名单的人，也许不是明确指定的，但鉴于您如此耐心地详述的所有情况，这是隐含其中的。我想向一位通讯员——约翰·巴尔先生——脱帽致敬。他有勇气签下自己的名字。如果您其他的通讯员中有人能模仿他，他们就会向我们披露他们是否真的拥有选票（在某些情况下我斗胆表示怀疑），而且他们可能也会像现在这样接近于讲出合乎常理的话。我只希望我能签下我的名字，因为我意识到匿名削弱了我的论点；但是，你知道为什么我不能。我最后只想说，我担心有些人觉得坐下来给报纸写“空话”比通过研究贵报社论中的论点来运用他们仅有的一点思考机制更容易。他们可能甚至不看背面所谓的独立候选人的名字就投下选票。

WRANGOO.
上海，3月22日。

“明显的闹剧”

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，终于有了人们……的迹象，要摆脱冬眠将是一件困难的事。然而，为什么要追究一个你我作为局外人都无法产生任何确切兴趣的话题呢。再喝一杯，让我们换个话题吧。”

先生，这段对话发生在大约十年前，由于英国社区在贵报来信专栏中对即将到来的觉醒表现出的惊人兴趣，它又回到了我的记忆中，但我几乎担心为时已晚，除非正确解读时代的迹象——他们迄今为止完全未加注意——打破“核心圈子”的垄断，让“普通人”有机会发出自己的声音。

P. K.
上海，3月22日。

撤回其候选人提名，以真正抗议正在以最“腐朽”的方式进行的所作所为。
我持有的另一个观点是：如果这些纳税人被要求投票支持的“大人物”憎恨这种不公平，他们要么停止对其他候选人进行的肮脏勾当，要么荣誉地从这场所谓的工部局选举的候选人名单中撤回他们的名字。
就英国居民而言，在我看来，他们的紧迫责任是将这件丑恶的事情提交给驻此地的总领事，或者向我国政府全面报告目前正在发生的“卑鄙”和可耻的行径。
人们津津乐道的英国正义在哪里？至少从目前的情况来看，这里没有。那些“遵守规则”、“光明磊落”、“公平公正”的运动精神言论在哪里？显然，对于像我这样在上海长期居住的人来说，这里也没有。

一位非常老的居民。
上海，3月21日。

休斯先生的候选资格

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，我以极大的兴趣阅读了今天贵刊上A. J. 休斯先生的来信。我一直钦佩这位在我们国际租界服务的老兵，并且在他参加工部局选举时总是投票给他。
如果我没记错的话，他此前曾有一两次被我们当地社区的一位知名人士提名为董事，我相信休斯先生下周又能指望得到犹太选民的选票。
他在今天贵刊上的来信使他的立场非常明确，几乎不需要再添加什么有利于他的内容来确保他获胜。赞扬他的出色工作并认可他的无私服务是公平的。他值得我们的信任，我希望上海能再次看到他担任这个本地国际议会的董事。

ISRAELITE.
上海，3月21日。

一个预言

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，很多年前，一位非常亲爱的英国朋友用一个问题让我大吃一惊：“K.，你为什么不竞选董事？你对公共事务有看法，而且我认为总体上是健全的看法，比如管弦乐队、电车、公共汽车等，你不时在《字林西报》上发表这些观点。你可以成为工部局中有用的一员，应该参加选举。”对此，我的回答大致如下：“亲爱的L.，首先，我不是英国人。其次，我不是那个迷人的核心圈子的成员，这个圈子由‘互相欣赏协会’得力地代表，其成员通过互相提名和附议来提供将要当选的董事。这个寡头集团自视为贵族阶层，像我这样的无名小卒进入工部局的机会并不比月中人更大。我不支持上海的骄傲，即世界上最长的吧台。我没有赛马，不举办派对，不常去俱乐部。换句话说，我不具备加入‘互相欣赏协会’的资格，因为追求这种抱负所需的主要特质在我身上都缺失了。选举的性质以及这里仍然沿用的制度，使得‘局外人’完全不可能参与。无论他在其他方面的资格多么高，除非他非常熟悉当地情况，并且充满了上海人精神，再加上……”

“一位新候选人”

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，关于贵报今早宝贵版面中题为“一位新候选人”的社论小品，我谨提出异议，无疑许多其他纳税人也持此看法。
首先，担任帝国化学工业公司（I.C.I.）负责人再次意味着既得利益，而这正是我们都不想要的。
再者，谁是我们的领袖？谁任命他们为领袖的？他们甚至代表了上海50%的英国居民吗？
当然，如果我们在这个城市有任何领袖的话，那必须是英王陛下的总领事，而不是那些有着私心要发泄的自封领袖。
此外，我不认为上过伊顿公学等学校有什么作用，能使我们的新候选人更受纳税人欢迎。我也曾就读于著名的苏格兰公立学校，在橄榄球苏格兰选拔赛中出场，也在圣安德鲁斯的高尔夫业余锦标赛中参赛，保持日本两个最佳球场的记录等等，但这并没有使我成为工部局董事的可能候选人。

特威德河以北。
上海，3月22日。

***不得不枯燥地解释令人沮丧：由于某些批评家声称基勒里先生的履历不为人知，因此按惯例发布了一份简短的生平简介。如果“特威德河以北”先生的运动倾向导致他专注于基勒里先生职业生涯的早期阶段，并阻碍了他对简介中提到的重要商业任命的意义的明智评价，那是必须归咎于苏格兰教育体系的缺陷。同样，投诉者未能理解一个简单的事实，即三个英国组织的执行委员会很难被称为“自封的”。它们是经过正式选举产生的。如果有人希望改变这样一种传统，即工部局董事通常包括在租界福利中有既定利害关系的公认地位人士，那么对“既得利益”的恐惧是可以理解的，但在负责任的观察者看来，这并不令人印象深刻。

中国人的观点

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，关于上海工部局目前的选举，让外国社区了解以下事实将具有普遍意义：除了《土地章程》规定的使纳税人有资格成为工部局成员的两项财产资格外，中国纳税人协会在向选民推荐中国候选人之前，还要求具备五年或以上的居住资格。
协会自1928年首次纳入华人代表时起制定并实施的《上海工部局华董选举规则》第二条规定如下：
“这些在国际租界居住五年或以上，并具备下列资格之一者，有资格当选为董事：(a) 每年纳税银50两或以上 (b) 除房捐外，每年支付租金银1,200两或以上。”
虽然《土地章程》排除了向工部局缴纳规定数额捐税但未在租界内“居住”的人成为选民或候选人的资格，但对于参加工部局投票的候选人，并没有规定具体的居住年限。
鉴于上海当地独有的、在世界上其他地方无与伦比的特殊性，有很多理由支持协会对其候选人施加的额外资格要求，这一事实，加之华人选举进行的谨慎和务实的方式，使得自工部局设立华人席位以来，推举出的参与市政管理的华人代表格外强大且能干。

一名中国旁观者。
上海，3月22日。

候选人声明
《字林西报》

致编辑先生：

所有工部局候选人都必须陈述其政纲——换言之，向选民明确陈述他们对管理租界的看法，这应该是强制性的。
选民完全不知道他们的代表如果当选将采取什么态度，这导致了投票的冷漠——例如，私人电话的问题从未被提及，然而，一个很少使用电话的小住户要提高捐税，而招待远超其一部电话应承载人数的寄宿公寓，按比例来说却处境好得多。
再者——我非常不喜欢攻击任何国籍，但根据我目前从这里了解到的情况，我们必须有一支受薪的俄罗斯人队伍加入义勇队编制，我们可以轻易找到足够多的英国人、美国人、德国人等，他们会非常乐意有机会取代这些人，我问你，俄罗斯人为建设这个国际租界做了什么？革命后这里仅仅成为了避难所，他们的涌入破坏了当地的劳动力市场。
让纳税人联合起来，说明他们期望候选人采取什么态度，并投票给符合这一要求的人。

纳税人。
上海，3月22日。

***按照最近的做法，候选人声明将于周日发布。

一项政纲

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，我是否可以建议，英国选民的冷漠（对此可能有抱怨）可能是由于整个社区对所谓的“领袖”缺乏信心。
无论对错，一段时间以来，在普通选民看来，工部局事务周围存在着一种令人不满的气氛，工部局本身几乎没有做什么来消除这种气氛，而这种不满是自然且正当的。
如果本次选举中的任何一位候选人敢于提出：
(1) 废除人力车附例
(2) 废除工部局管弦乐队
(3) 对电话问题进行独立调查
我想，他很有可能在票数上名列前茅。

CIVIS BRITANNICUS.
上海，3月22日。

MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS
"Harmful" Procedure

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—May I refer to your leading article in the "North-China" of March 21, "British Apathy".

As a British ratepayer I raise my voice in protest at the procedure of the committees of the British Residents' Association and kindred societies expressing the wishes of hundreds of their members without even having called a meeting and getting their expression of opinion as to who are suitable as British members for the next Municipal Council Election.

It appears to me a reflection on the intelligence of British ratepayers.

Had the names of candidates been placed before the members of these associations the result for the British ticket might have been totally different.

The whole procedure is contrary to British fair play and democratic principles, and we Britons pride ourselves on belonging to the most democratic race in the world.

I feel the whole procedure has been harmful, and British ratepayers may indeed show their "British Apathy" to which you refer in your leading article.

I have my own views and claim the right as a British ratepayer to use my own judgment. BRITISH FAIR PLAY.
Shanghai, Mar. 21.

“有害的”程序

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生——请允许我提及贵报3月21日题为《英国人的冷漠》的社论。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, MARCH 22, 1935
10277

Revival Wanted

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—Your Leader of to-day's date anent British Apathy relative to the coming Election, was to my mind a part-eulogy of the Japanese and their election ardour as contrasted with the British Electorates' apparent indifference. Have you ever troubled to seek the reason of this indifference? I would say, in part, that it is chiefly due to the spirit of condescension which is so manifest in the attitude adopted by the three British organizations to which you refer, when dealing with the ordinary rank and file.
"They are well-provided with machinery for giving their views an opportunity of expression", you write, but, do they? I think not! The well-worn expressions "Convention" and "Constitution" also get honourable mention, but strange to say the correlative of these words "un" is even unplaced. But isn't it unconventional and unconstitutional for Candidates to elect to seek election without even telling the Public what they stand for?

This prefix "un" could be adopted to quite a multiple of words having a direct bearing on the situation; words such as unsympathetic, unsystematic, antisocial, unsaid—the last being the chief reason for the general apathy pertaining to things municipal, for, so much was left unsaid which might have been told to advantage.

If it were possible to obtain a drop of an elector's blood for analysis it would probably require a magnification of 1,000, ere the bacilli of an election germ were found.

This indifference, too, might be explained by a well-known psychological fact, that a man will fight hard to obtain something desired but having got possession of it, will lose interest, until another fight looms in which he is threatened with extinction. Was this the underlying motive which actuated the B.R.A. in circularizing their members through the various Societies? Was it just another straw showing which way the wind is blowing?

The British are too prone to rely upon the Biblical quotation, "The meek shall inherit the earth" or, at any rate, that section of the British people who are domiciled in Shanghai appear to think so.

According to an old Moslem belief, when the Day of Judgment is near, the Angel Israfil will blow three blasts upon his trumpet, viz. Blast of Confusion, Blast of Inquiry, Blast of Resurrection. It is to be hoped that the S.M.C. election of 1935 will sound the Blast of Resurrection, in so far, as it relates to the lack of interest of the British Electorate.

This letter is in no way condemnatory of the British Residents en masse, but is merely a pointer to the British Residents Association with their affiliated Societies, showing the way, that a reversal of policy is necessary, if the British interests are to be maintained in the lead here.

DE PROFUNDIS.
Shanghai, Mar. 21.

《字林西报》，1935年3月22日，星期五
10277

呼吁复兴

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生——贵报今日关于即将到来的选举中英国人冷漠态度的社论，在我看来说是对日本人及其选举热情的一种部分颂扬，并与英国选民表面上的漠不关心形成对比。您是否曾费心去探究这种冷漠的原因？我想说，部分原因主要在于您所提到的三个英国组织在对待普通大众时所采取的态度中表现出的那种居高临下的精神。
您写道：“他们拥有完善的机制来让他们的观点得到表达的机会”，但是，真的如此吗？我认为并非如此！那些陈词滥调般的“惯例”和“章程”也得到了体面的提及，但奇怪的是，这些词的反义前缀“un-（非/不）”甚至未被放置。但是，候选人在甚至不向公众说明其立场的情况下就决定寻求当选，这难道不是不合惯例且违宪的吗？

这个前缀“un-”可以加在许多与当前局势直接相关的词语上；例如缺乏同情心（unsympathetic）、无系统性（unsystematic）、反社会（antisocial）、未言明（unsaid）——最后一个是导致人们对市政事务普遍冷漠的主要原因，因为许多本可以有利地告知公众的事情却被留白未说。

如果有可能提取一滴选民的血液进行分析，可能需要放大1000倍，才能发现选举热情的病菌。

这种冷漠也可以用众所周知的心理学事实来解释，即一个人会为了获得渴望之物而努力奋斗，但一旦拥有，就会失去兴趣，直到另一次威胁到其生存的斗争出现。这是否是英国居民协会通过各个社团向其成员发出通告背后的潜在动机？这是否只是显示风向的另一根稻草？

英国人过于倾向于依赖《圣经》中的引文：“温柔的人必承受地土”，或者至少，居住在上海的那部分英国人似乎是这么认为的。

根据一种古老的穆斯林信仰，当审判日临近时，天使伊斯拉菲尔（Israfil）将吹响他的号角三次，即：混乱之号、询问之号、复活之号。希望1935年的工部局选举能吹响复活之号，就此而言，它是针对英国选民缺乏兴趣这一状况的。

这封信绝非对全体英国居民的谴责，而仅仅是为英国居民协会及其附属社团指出方向，表明如果要保持英国利益在此处的领先地位，就必须扭转政策。

DE PROFUNDIS（出自深渊）。
上海，3月21日。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, MARCH 22, 1935
10276

“Astounding Attitude”

To the Editor of the
“NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS”

SIR,—The attitude adopted in your leading articles of yesterday and to-day and also by the Committees of the British Chamber and Associations is really astounding.

A scrutiny of the names of those recommended by the Committees for election and also of their proposers and seconders shows that all of these gentlemen come under one or more of the categories below:—

1. Members of the Committees of the bodies mentioned.
2. Present or recent members of the Council
3. Very close business associates of each other.

It is, therefore, clear that “MAXTONITE’S” references to a “family party” and “blue-eyed boys” are fully justified; it is obvious that anyone not in the family will not be tolerated by the existing members and their friends unless invited by them as in the instance of the nominee who has a bare eighteen months residence in China to his credit. For the Committees of the British associations to attempt to exclude from this party a nominee who has the audacity to go up for election is a most remarkable attitude.

True, the Japanese and American communities have come to a decision as to the candidates of their own nationalities that they would support, but they arrived at this decision before the nominations were sent in. Apathy among the British there perhaps is, further evidence of this would appear to show itself in the action of the Committees—leaders I think you call them—in not having made their arrangements earlier and thus avoiding the need for all this public laundry work. Unity of opinion taken by a pre-nomination vote among all B.R.A. members or Britons would ensure solidarity and unity of purpose.

But if we are to be “committee controlled” why bother to have an Election at all? The voting becomes a mere farce and a game of “follow my leader”. This will tend to make the ordinary man even more apathetic, he will realize that the Councillors are appointed by invitation and that it is a waste of time to go to the booths.

In the past there have been vigorous Election campaigns in the course of which so-called intruders have successfully broken the ring and secured election to the benefit of the Council and the community.

Let those who vote do so as their own opinions dictate and refuse to be coerced into automatic action.

BRITISH RATEPAYER.
Shanghai, Mar. 21.

《字林西报》，1935年3月22日，星期五
10276

“惊人的态度”

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生——贵报昨日和今日的社论以及英国商会和各协会委员会所采取的态度确实令人震惊。

仔细审查各委员会推荐当选的人员名单，以及他们的提名人和附议人，可以看出所有这些绅士都属于以下一个或多个类别：—

1. 上述机构的委员会成员。
2. 现任或近期的董事会成员。
3. 彼此之间非常紧密的商业伙伴。

因此，显然“MAXTONITE”所指称的“家族派对”和“宠儿”是完全有道理的；显而易见，除非受到现有成员及其朋友的邀请，否则任何不属于这个“家族”的人都不会被容忍，就像那位仅有十八个月在华居住记录的提名人那样。英国各协会的委员会试图将一名大胆参加选举的提名人排除在这个党派之外，这是一种极为惊人的态度。

诚然，日本和美国社区已经就支持其本国国籍的候选人做出了决定，但他们在提交提名之前就已做出此决定。英国人中或许存在冷漠，委员会——我想您称他们为领袖——的行动似乎进一步证明了这一点，他们没有更早地做出安排，从而避免了所有这些公开洗白工作的需要。如果在所有英国居民协会成员或英国人中进行提名前投票以达成意见统一，将确保团结和目标一致。

但是，如果我们都要受“委员会控制”，那又何必举行选举呢？投票变成了一场纯粹的闹剧和一场“跟我做”的游戏。这将使普通人更加冷漠，他会意识到董事是由邀请任命的，去投票站是浪费时间。

过去曾有过激烈的竞选活动，在此期间，所谓的闯入者成功打破了圈子并当选，这对董事会和社区都有利。

让投票者按照自己的意愿投票，拒绝被胁迫进行自动化的行动。

英国纳税人。
上海，3月21日。

10375

NOT "NIT-WITS"
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
SIR,—Being a member of the British Residents' Association, China Association, and the British Chamber of Commerce, I would like to express through the medium of your columns my extreme disapproval of the amazing temerity of the Committees announcement exhorting British voters to support certain candidates in the forthcoming Municipal elections.
This recommending, or shall I say, almost demanding, that Britons go in force to the Polls and plump for their selection, conveys the impression that a coterie of interested parties are determined to have their special interests represented because they fear that some candidate or candidates are not as popular among certain voters of both British and other nationalities, to ensure their return without this form of propaganda.
It has been stated that Britons who do not exercise their vote and assert themselves at the Polls will, by their lack of interest, be regarded as "reprehensible." May I emphasize that this method of electioneering and throwing cold water on two other nominees, namely, Mr. A. J. Hughes and Mr. Mr. L. Hossenlopp, is about the most "reprehensible" procedure that has come within my purview. I, therefore, hope that Mr. A. J. Hughes and Mr. L. Hossenlopp will not withdraw from the contest as I can assure them that I shall plump for these two candidates and sincerely hope that many other independent Britons who have votes will do the same.
After all, why should the British voters be regarded as "nit-wits" to be led by the nose, or shall we say, third degree, by any small group of voters as though they were unable independently to think and decide for themselves? Shanghai has outgrown the stage when employers could almost compel their employees to vote as they desired.
INDEPENDENT.
Shanghai, March 21, 1935.

10375

并非“傻瓜”
编辑，
《上海泰晤士报》
先生——作为英国居民协会、中国协会和英国商会的成员，我想通过贵报专栏表达我对各委员会公告中令人惊异的鲁莽行为的极度不满，该公告敦促英国选民在即将到来的市政选举中支持某些候选人。
这种推荐，或者我该说，几乎是要求英国人大举前往投票站并集中投票支持他们选定的人选，给人的印象是，一群利益相关者决心让他们的特殊利益得到代表，因为他们担心如果没有这种形式的宣传，某些候选人在某些英国及其他国籍的选民中不够受欢迎，无法确保当选。
有人声称，不行使投票权并在投票站主张自身权利的英国人，将因其缺乏兴趣而被视为“应受谴责”。我要强调，这种竞选方法以及对另外两名提名人，即 A. J. Hughes 先生和 L. Hossenlopp 先生泼冷水的做法，是我所见过的最“应受谴责”的程序。因此，我希望 A. J. Hughes 先生和 L. Hossenlopp 先生不要退出竞争，因为我可以向他们保证，我将集中投票支持这两位候选人，并真诚希望许多其他拥有投票权的独立英国人也这样做。
毕竟，为什么英国选民应被视为可以被任何小团体牵着鼻子走，或者可以说，遭受严刑逼供般的对待的“傻瓜”，仿佛他们无法独立思考和为自己做决定？上海已经超越了雇主几乎可以强迫雇员按其意愿投票的阶段。
独立人士。
上海，1935年3月21日。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, MARCH 22, 1935 .

/ S. James
ELECTION QUERIES
Editor, 22.3.35
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—Notices sponsored by the British Residents' Association and the British Chamber of Commerce are now appearing in the papers exhorting British ratepayers to vote solid for certain gentlemen at the forthcoming Municipal Election. Suspending our independent judgment—not that we are likely to be granted much information on which to base such a judgment—we are to vote the whole "ticket," regardless of the fact that we probably know little about the views or abilities of many of those named. Leaving aside, however, the general question of the desirability of this "ticket" innovation, and the presumption involved in its presentation, I would like to ask certain questions.
1.—At what meeting of the British Residents' Association was it decided to issue these instructions to British voters? How many members were present and who were they?
2.—What authority has the British Residents' Association to speak in this way for British ratepayers? How many were present at its last annual general meeting, and by what percentage of its members was the present committee elected?
3.—To what extent can the Chamber of Commerce be said to be representative of British opinion? For whom does it speak beyond a few of the larger commercial interests?
4.—To what extent is the British Residents' Association merely the British Chamber of Commerce under another name? One notices that they both have the same Secretary and issue their notices from the same office.
5.—Who is Mr. V. St. J. Killery recommended to the voters? How long has he been in Shanghai and what experience has he had of local conditions?
6.—Would it be impertinent to inquire into the business connections and associations of those recommended to us? One hears and reads in the course of one's daily round many dark references to "vested interests," and one would like to have the apprehensions aroused thereby set at rest—as of course they can be.
A. W. K. WARD.
Shanghai, March 21, 1935.

先生——由英国居民协会和英国商会赞助的公告现在出现在报纸上，敦促英国纳税人在即将到来的市政选举中团结一致投票支持某些绅士。暂停我们的独立判断——并不是说我们很可能获得多少基于此类判断的信息——我们要对整个“名单”进行投票，不管我们可能对许多被提名者的观点或能力知之甚少这一事实。然而，撇开这种“名单”创新的可取性这一普遍问题及其提出时所涉及的傲慢不谈，我想问几个问题。
1.—英国居民协会是在哪次会议上决定向英国选民发布这些指示的？有多少成员出席，他们是谁？
2.—英国居民协会有何权力以这种方式代表英国纳税人发言？在其上次年度股东大会上有多少人出席，现任委员会是由百分之多少的成员选举产生的？
3.—在多大程度上可以说商会代表了英国舆论？除了少数大型商业利益集团外，它还为谁发声？
4.—英国居民协会在多大程度上只是换了个名字的英国商会？人们注意到，两者拥有相同的秘书，并从同一办公室发布公告。
5.—推荐给选民的 V. St. J. Killery 先生是谁？他在上海待了多久，对当地情况有什么经验？
6.—调查被推荐给我们的那些人的商业联系和关联是否显得无礼？在日常活动中，人们听到并读到许多关于“既得利益”的晦暗暗示，人们希望由此引起的担忧得以消除——当然它们是可以消除的。
A. W. K. WARD。
上海，1935年3月21日。

MORE DISAPPROVAL
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—May I join with your two correspondents—"British Voter" and "Won't Vote"—who protested in this morning's paper against the action of the Committees of the B.R.A., the British Chamber of Commerce and the China Association in picking out a "ticket" from among the candidates standing for election to the S.M.C.
I am also a member of the B.R.A. but I do not think that the Committee was ever authorized to do what it has now done, and I much resent the picking out of some men for support and the leaving out of another who is a fellow member with me in the Association.
There is far too much of this "inner control" in Shanghai, and I think it very largely accounts for the apathy of the general electorate. At any rate, it causes me to sign myself,
FED UP.
Shanghai, March 21, 1935.

A VOTER'S PROTEST
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
SIR,—I shall be hoping to see some protest other than my own at the action taken by the Committees of the three leading British associations here in trespassing on the rights of the electorate to make a free choice of Councillors from the men who have been nominated. Can it be considered ethical for Committeemen to meet in secret and without warrant from their members to make up a "ticket" and then to spend some of the funds of their organizations in urging electors to vote for certain men, to the exclusion of at least one man who is a member of one or more of those organizations? To put it as low as possible, it is a piece of cheek. All that these men have a right to is their own personal opinions, and to elevate those opinions to the status of an "official" injunction is unprecedented and quite unwarranted.
I am told that the idea is to get British voters to show their strength in solid form; to impress on other nationals the fact that British voting strength can be marshalled against any possible threat of a challenge. So far so good. But I am also told that it was really desired to avoid an election at all this year, that it was understood that Mr. Hughes would not go up if there were enough other candidates. Now, which is it? If it is desired to show solidarity then those now not included in the "favoured five" ought to be thanked for daring to stand and be made targets of; if no election was wanted how could a show of solidarity have been made?
Frankly, I am puzzled; but I am also amazed at the action of a coterie of men, unbidden, daring publicly to be our mentors on what, in the absence of any electioneering statements, must be a question of purely personal choice.
BRITISH VOTER.
Shanghai, March 20, 1935.

BRITISHER COMPLAINS
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
SIR,—I have been a resident of Shanghai for 15 years and, for the past nine, have been a ratepayer. Each year, I have tried to take what might be termed an "intelligent interest" in elections for the Municipal Council. Possibly my intelligence has not been up to the standard of those who aim at controlling everything in the Settlement, including the votes of the British members of the community.
I am also a member of the British Residents' Association since it was first started and am a believer in British freedom. But when it comes to being told what I shall do and what I must not do by a bunch of committee-men, I naturally raise my feeble voice in protest.
According to an advertisement in your paper this morning, British voters are urged to vote for five candidates selected by some persons on the British Residents' Association, British Chamber of Commerce and China Association. Of the five British candidates named, three of them are members of the committee of the British Residents' Association — Messrs. Harold Porter, H. E. Arnhold and V. St. J. Killery—Mr. Porter is also Chairman of the B. R. A. The other two, Messrs. Liddell and W. P. Lambe, I'm not concerned about.
Does it mean that Mr. Porter, as Chairman of the B. R. A., and Messrs. Arnhold and Killery, committee members, have held a little get-together in the Club and, by virtue of their positions, have endorsed themselves as the best candidates for Municipal honours? It looks that way to me.
WON'T VOTE.
Shanghai, March 20, 1935.

《字林西报》编辑
先生，——我希望看到除我本人之外，还有其他抗议声音，反对本地三大主要英人协会委员会所采取的行动，即侵犯选民权利，使其无法从被提名人选中自由挑选董事。委员们在未获其成员授权的情况下秘密集会，拟定一份“候选人名单”，随后动用其组织部分资金，敦促选民投票支持特定人选，而将至少一名属于这些组织中一个或多个组织的成员排除在外，这种做法难道能被视为合乎道德吗？往最轻里说，这是一种厚颜无耻的行为。这些人唯一有权拥有的只是他们个人的意见，而将这些意见提升到具有“官方”命令的地位，则是史无前例且毫无根据的。
我听说，此举意在让英国选民以团结一致的姿态展示其力量；向其他国籍人士表明，英国人的投票力量可以集结起来，应对任何可能出现的挑战威胁。至此尚属合理。但我还听说，实际上今年根本希望避免举行选举，据称大家已达成默契，如果有足够的其他候选人，休斯先生（Mr. Hughes）就不会参选。那么，究竟是哪一种情况？如果意在展示团结，那么那些目前未被列入“受青睐的五人”名单的人，应当因其敢于站出来成为众矢之的而受到感谢；如果本不希望举行选举，又怎能展示出团结的姿态呢？
坦率地说，我感到困惑；但我也对一小撮人的行为感到震惊，他们在无人邀请的情况下，竟敢公开充当我们的导师，就一个在缺乏任何竞选陈述的情况下纯属个人选择的问题指手画脚。
英国选民。
上海，1935年3月20日。

英籍人士投诉
致：
《字林西报》编辑
先生，——我在上海居住已有15年，并在过去九年中一直是纳税人。每年，我都试图对工部局董事会选举表现出一种可称为“明智的关注”。也许我的智慧达不到那些旨在控制租界内一切事务（包括英籍社区成员的选票）的人的标准。
我也是自英国侨民协会成立之初便加入的会员，并且信奉英式自由。但是，当一群委员会成员告诉我该做什么和不该做什么时，我自然要发出微弱的抗议之声。
根据今早贵报刊登的一则广告，英国选民被敦促投票支持由英国侨民协会、上海英国商会和中国协会（Shanghai Branch of the China Association）某些人士选出的五名候选人。在被提名的五名英国候选人中，有三名是英国侨民协会委员会的成员——哈罗德·波特（Harold Porter）、H. E. 阿诺尔德（H. E. Arnhold）和 V. St. J. 基勒里（V. St. J. Killery）先生——波特先生还是英国侨民协会主席。另外两位，利德尔（Liddell）和 W. P. 兰姆（W. P. Lambe）先生，我不予置评。
这是否意味着，作为英国侨民协会主席的波特先生，以及作为委员的阿诺尔德和基勒里先生，在俱乐部里搞了一次小聚会，并凭借其职位身份，自我背书为获取工部局荣誉的最佳候选人？在我看来，情况似乎正是如此。
不投票者。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 20, 1935

S.M.C. ELECTION
Mr. Hossenlopp's View

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—From the early days of the
Settlement voters have refused to
vote en-bloc. They have by various
means been able to assess the
qualities and qualifications of candi-
dates who have presented themselves
and have rightly refused to elect a
candidate who has been tried and
found wanting.
The Council, at considerable ex-
pense, engaged Mr. Justice Richard
Feetham. In his very comprehensive
study of the Settlement the eminent
jurist points out in one of several
volumes, that this is an International
Settlement we reside in and not a
Foreign Settlement as many think.
In an international settlement interna-
tional partnership should be aimed at.
At considerable pains the eminent
jurist places on record that from 1854
onwards, the American community
usually has been represented by at
least one member. From 1873 to 1914
there was always one German mem-
ber of Council. For each of the ten
years from 1879 to 1888 the Council
included either a French or Danish
member. From 1890 to 1914 the
Council normally consisted of seven
British members, one American, and
one German member. When the
German member dropped out at the
end of 1914, his place was taken by
a Russian member. The Russian
member dropped out at the end of
1918. The Japanese representation
was increased from one to two mem-
bers in 1927, and the American re-
presentation has been normally two
members since 1919. In 1930 six
British members were elected and
only one American, owing to the fact
that three American candidates went
to the poll, and there was some un-
certainty as to which were the two
who were to be regarded as repre-
senting the choice of the American
community. In 1931 the position was
restored; the Americans again obtain-
ed two members, and the number of
British members was reduced to five.
Since then it will be recalled Capt.
Bahnsen, a Dane, secured a seat on
the Council.
There is precedent for the election
of a French citizen.
Ratepayers elect men to the
Council to run the Settlement and to
improve conditions and not as various
national representatives.
It is my intention to state my aims
and what I stand for and a later date
and to rely on the broad-mindedness
of the ratepayers of the International
Settlement.
L. R. HOSSENLOPP.
Shanghai, Mar. 19.

工部局选举
霍森洛普先生的观点

致《字林西报》编辑

先生，——自租界早期以来，选民一直拒绝集体投票（en-bloc）。他们通过各种方式能够评估候选人的品质和资格，并正确地拒绝选举那些经过考验但被认为不合格的候选人。
工部局花费巨资聘请了理查德·费瑟姆法官（Mr. Justice Richard Feetham）。这位著名法学家在其对租界的详尽研究中，在其中一卷中指出，我们居住的是一个国际租界，而非许多人认为的外国租界。在一个国际租界中，应以国际合作为目标。这位著名法学家煞费苦心地记录道，自1854年以来，美侨社区通常至少有一名代表。从1873年到1914年，董事会中始终有一名德籍董事。在1879年至1888年的十年间，董事会每年均包括一名法籍或丹籍董事。从1890年到1914年，董事会通常由七名英籍、一名美籍和一名德籍董事组成。当1914年底德籍董事退出后，其席位由一名俄籍董事接替。该俄籍董事于1918年底退出。日籍代表人数在1927年从一人增加至两人，而自1919年以来，美籍代表通常为两人。1930年，由于三名美国候选人参加投票，且对于哪两位应被视为代表美侨社区的选择存在某种不确定性，因此选出了六名英籍董事，而美籍仅有一名。1931年，这一状况得以恢复；美国人再次获得两个席位，英籍董事人数减少至五人。此后，人们会记得，丹麦人巴恩森上尉（Capt. Bahnsen）在董事会中获得了一个席位。
选举法国公民是有先例的。
纳税人选举人士进入董事会是为了管理租界并改善状况，而不是作为各国籍的代表。
我打算在稍后日期陈述我的目标和立场，并依靠国际租界纳税人的开明态度。
L. R. 霍森洛普（L. R. HOSSENLOPP）。
上海，3月19日。

Leon Robert Hossenlopp was born in the province
of Alsace-Lorraine, France. He is of German extraction
but became a French citizen following the province being
retroceded to France in 1919.
Some number of years ago he was in Australia
where he was employed as a chef at different hotels. On
leaving that country he proceeded to India where he obtained
a position as Manager of the Taj Mahal Hotel, Bombay. This
position he held until 1925 when he left India for Shanghai.
On March 11, 1926, Hossenlopp took over the
"Marcel" restaurant, 242/6 Szechuen Road, and later in that
year removed to the present premises at No.102 Nanking
Road.
Prior to the Municipal election in 1934 he wrote
a letter to the Evening Post & Mercury suggesting that the
Council should enquire into the antecedents of prospective
candidates. This was undoubtedly directed against Beaumont
who had swindled him out of a sum of money some time previous.
Hossenloff is regarded as a quick tempered individual
and is always experiencing trouble with his employees but
apart from this there is nothing known to his detriment.
About 3 years ago he married a Russian named
Miss E. N. Jukova who was cashier at Marcels.

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY , MARCH 17, 1935.

STATUS OF
SETTLEMENT
DESCRIBED

Writer Reviews Decade
Here; Taipan Control
Is Condemned

THE INTERNATIONAL SETTLE-
MENT AT SHANGHAI, by Wil-
liam W. Lockwood, Jr., pp. 17.

This publication by Professor Lock-
wood of Bowdoin College is a re-
print of an article in The American
Political Science Review (Vol.
XXVIII, No. 6, December, 1934).
It deals largely with the history of
the International Settlement of
Shanghai during the decade 1924-
1934. Most of the facts dealt with
are familiar to local residents and
for that reason do not call for ex-
tended comment. But for those
who do not live in Shanghai, the
pamphlet should make interesting
reading.

He points out such obvious facts
as that "the Council membership,
foreign and Chinese, is drawn very
largely from the ranks of big busi-
ness" and that "the municipal re-
gime as at present constituted re-
mains highly oligarchical in charac-
ter." He also mentions the "halt-
ing acceptance" of the civic point
of view, by the foreign community
as a result of which Chinese were
admitted to the municipal parks
and also increased appropriations
were made to the schools, particu-
larly those for Chinese. But appar-
ently Professor Lockwood is not
highly impressed with our "Model
Settlement" for he asks the ques-
tion "model for whom?"

There is some rather caustic com-
ment upon industrial conditions in
Shanghai where "unbridled exploita-
tion exists in its rankest forms." He
also observes "that this large indus-
trial center is totally devoid of fac-
tory regulations except for a few
building rules and fire regulations."
He points out that "The Interna-
tional Settlement authorities were
long apathetic toward factory
reform which the champions of the
movement had referred to in 1933
as 'the ghost of communism.'"

Considering the fact that Profes-
sor Lockwood was treated rather
badly by the Japanese authorities as
he passed through Japan on his way
to America from China last year,
he deals rather gently with them in
connection with their enormous des-
truction of life and property in
Shanghai in 1932. Reference is
made, however, to the fact that
Japanese forces did usurp the au-
thority of the Municipal Council.

As to the conclusions reached in
his study of the International Set-
tlement, the Bowdoin professor
states: "Politically and economical-
ly, the status of Shanghai is one of
unstable equilibrium." After refer-
ring to the industrialization and
westernization in treaty port areas,
which is furtherest advanced in
Shanghai, he adds: "It creates is-
sues of local and national economic
policy which are settled by aimless
drift in the absence of conscious
control."

This analysis of local political
and social conditions by a professor
of political science is, despite the
restraint which he exercises in his
language, essentially an indictment
of the administration of one of the
great cities of the world or at
least that part of it controlled by
the foreign taipans.—J. B. P.

作者回顾此地十年历程；谴责大班控制

《上海国际租界》，小威廉·W. 洛克伍德（William W. Lockwood, Jr.）著，共17页。

这本由鲍登学院（Bowdoin College）洛克伍德教授出版的刊物，是重印自《美国政治科学评论》（The American Political Science Review，第XXVIII卷，第6期，1934年12月）的一篇文章。它主要论述了1924-1934年这十年间上海国际租界的历史。所涉及的大部分事实为本地居民所熟悉，因此无需过多评论。但对于不住在上海的人来说，这本小册子读起来应该颇有趣味。

他指出了一些显而易见的事实，如“董事会成员，无论外籍还是华籍，很大程度上选自大商界”，以及“目前的市政体制仍然具有高度的寡头政治特征”。他还提到，外侨社区对市民观点的“勉强接受”，由此导致华人得以进入市政公园，并且对学校（特别是华童学校）的拨款有所增加。但显然，洛克伍德教授对我们的“模范租界”印象并不深刻，因为他提出了“谁的模范？”这一问题。

文中对上海的工业状况有一些相当尖刻的评论，指出那里“存在着最猖獗形式的无节制剥削”。他还观察到，“这个大型工业中心完全缺乏工厂法规，除了一些建筑规则和消防规定外”。他指出，“国际租界当局长期以来对工厂改革漠不关心，而这场运动的倡导者在1933年将其称为‘共产主义的幽灵’。”

鉴于洛克伍德教授去年从中国途经日本前往美国时受到日本当局的恶劣对待，他在提及日军1932年在上海造成的大规模生命财产损失时，措辞较为温和。然而，文中确实提到了日军确实篡夺了工部局的权力这一事实。

关于他对国际租界研究得出的结论，这位鲍登学院的教授 stating：“在政治和经济上，上海的地位处于一种不稳定的平衡状态。”在提到通商口岸地区的工业化和西化（以上海最为先进）之后，他补充道：“这在缺乏有意识控制的情况下，通过漫无目的的漂移，造成了地方和国家经济政策方面的问题。”

这位政治学教授对当地政治和社会状况的分析，尽管他在语言上保持了克制，但本质上是对这个世界大城市之一，或者至少是其受外国大班控制部分的行政管理的控诉。——J. B. P.

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, MARCH 17, 1935

S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 6590
Date / / 35

Five New Candidates To
Seek S.M. Council Seats
At Forthcoming Election

Two Of “Old Brigade” Are Not Seeking Re-election;
Eleven Nominations For Nine Available Seats;
One Frenchman Standing

JAPANESE ARE ONLY RUNNING FOR TWO
SEATS DESPITE EARLY RUMOURS

With eleven candidates nominated for the nine foreign seats on the Shanghai Municipal Council, an election is now assured. Six British, two American, two Japanese and one French candidate have signified their willingness to serve on the Council, if elected. Nominations closed yesterday noon with the Secretary of the S.M.C. and the names of candidates were awaited with considerable interest in view of the fact that rumours had been current that the Japanese were seeking additional representation and, also, that two of the present Councillors had indicated their intention to withdraw from office for private reasons. With the exception of the nomination of the French candidate and the re-appearance in the municipal arena of one of the former members, the nominations occasioned no surprise.

The following persons have been proposed and seconded, and have given their written consent to serve, if elected, as members of the Council for the Foreign Settlement of Shanghai for the Municipal year 1935:

| Candidate | Proposer | Seconder |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| H. E. Arnhold* | A. W. Burkill | N. L. Sparke |
| J. W. Carney* | P. S. Hopkins | C. E. Patton |
| C. S. Franklin* | A. Bassett | C. H. French |
| L. R. Hossenlopp | F. L. Hough | C. N. Gray |
| A. J. Hughes | N. G. Beale | J. W. Carney |
| V. St. J. Killery | B. D. F. Beith | A. W. Burkill |
| W. P. Lambe* | B. D. F. Beith | A. W. Burkill |
| J. H. Liddell* | A. D. Bell | A. W. Burkill |
| H. Porter, C.M.G. | N. L. Sparke | E. F. Harris |
| T. Urabe | K. Sugimoto | M. Yonesato |
| T. Yamamoto* | K. Sugimoto | M. Yonesato |

The poll will take place on Monday and Tuesday, March 25 and 26, from 10 a.m. until 3 p.m. Polling will take place at the Administration Building, 209 Kiangse Road, ground floor, and at the Hongkew Police Station.

No voting tickets will be sent out, qualified persons desiring to vote are required to attend at the polling booths, where the requisite voting tickets will be handed them. In order to avoid congestion at the polling booths, voters are requested to cast their votes as early as possible.

**Two Stand Down**

Of the eleven candidates who are offering their services to administer the Settlement in the coming municipal year, four are newcomers to the Council field while the fifth has occupied a seat at the Council table on previous occasions. All the new candidates, however, have served in various Council committees at different times, and all have been associated to some extent in Council activities during the past year.

Two well-known figures will be missed from the Council Chamber when the new group of civic fathers take office after the annual meeting of ratepayers. Mr. E. B. Macnaghten, chairman of the outgoing Council and for many years a prominent figure in civic affairs, will not be a candidate on this occasion as he is proceeding to England on long leave.

For the same reason Mr. E. F. Harris, also a member of the present Council will not be a candidate.

Messrs. Arnhold (Chairman) J. W. Carney, C. S. Franklin, W. P. Lambe, J. H. Liddell and T. Yamamoto, all members of the present Council, will seek a further term of office. Of this number three are British, two are American and one is a Japanese member.

The newcomers are three members of the British community in Messrs. Porter, Killery and Hughes, Mr. Hossenlopp is French and Mr. Urabe is a Japanese member of the community.

The proportion of representation on the present Council is five British members, two American and two Japanese. With the introduction of a French candidate and an additional British candidate the outcome of the pending elections is awaited with considerable interest.

**Men Of Affairs**

Mr. A. J. Hughes is actually no newcomer to Council affairs having served on the Council previously and subsequently acted on various Council committees. He is manager of the China United Assurance Society, Ltd.

Mr. L. R. Hossenlopp has not identified himself with municipal affairs in the Settlement previously, but has been a member of the Orchestra and Band Committee of the S.M.C. He is proprietor of the well-known Marcel establishments in the city.

Mr. V. St. J. Killery is also a comparative newcomer to local civic administration, but has been a member of the S.M.C. Traffic Committee during the past year. He is managing director of Imperial Chemical Industries, Ltd.

Mr. Harold Porter C.M.G. is offering himself for election as a Councillor for the first time, but has been a member of the Rates Assessment of the S.M.C. during the past year. He is a well-known local business man, for many years associated with the Pekin Syndicate.

Mr. T. Urabe, apart from being a member of the Works Committee has not hitherto been identified with local municipal affairs. He is manager of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha.

For some time prior to the announcement of nominations, it was freely reported that the Japanese community would seek an additional representative on the Council, and although opinion was divided regarding the advisability of raising this issue at the next election, there was still some doubt regarding the number of Japanese candidates until the nominations were disclosed at noon yesterday. Only two candidates are to represent the Japanese community.

**Land Commission**

Mr. H. G. F. Robinson, having been proposed by Mr. N. L. Sparke and seconded by Mr. A. W. Burkill, is, in accordance with Article VIA of the Land Regulations, considered to be elected a Land Commissioner for the Municipal Year 1935.

五名新候选人将
在即将举行的选举中
角逐工部局董事席位

两名“老资格”人士不寻求连任；
九个空缺席位共有十一人提名；
一名法国人参选

尽管早有传闻，日本人仅竞选两个席位

随着上海公共租界工部局九个外籍董事席位共有十一名候选人获得提名，选举现已确定无疑。六名英国人、两名美国人、两名日本人和一名法国籍候选人已表示，若当选，愿意在工部局任职。昨天中午，向工部局秘书处的提名截止，鉴于此前一直有传闻称日本人正寻求增加代表名额，且现任董事中有两人因私人原因示意有意辞职，候选人的名单备受各界关注。除了一名法国候选人的提名以及一名前成员重返市政舞台外，此次提名并未引起太多意外。

以下人员已被提名和附议，并已书面同意，若在1935市政年度当选，将担任上海公共租界工部局董事：

| 候选人 | 提名人 | 附议人 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| H. E. Arnhold* | A. W. Burkill | N. L. Sparke |
| J. W. Carney* | P. S. Hopkins | C. E. Patton |
| C. S. Franklin* | A. Bassett | C. H. French |
| L. R. Hossenlopp | F. L. Hough | C. N. Gray |
| A. J. Hughes | N. G. Beale | J. W. Carney |
| V. St. J. Killery | B. D. F. Beith | A. W. Burkill |
| W. P. Lambe* | B. D. F. Beith | A. W. Burkill |
| J. H. Liddell* | A. D. Bell | A. W. Burkill |
| H. Porter, C.M.G. | N. L. Sparke | E. F. Harris |
| T. Urabe | K. Sugimoto | M. Yonesato |
| T. Yamamoto* | K. Sugimoto | M. Yonesato |

投票将于3月25日（星期一）和26日（星期二）上午10时至下午3时进行。投票地点设在江西路209号行政大楼底层，以及虹口巡捕房。

选票不会寄出，符合资格的选民如需投票，须亲自前往投票站，届时将向其发放必要的选票。为避免投票站拥挤，请选民尽早投票。

**两人退选**

在十一位愿在下一个市政年度为租界管理效力的人选中，四人是工部局选举领域的新人，而第五人曾在此前担任过工部局董事。然而，所有新候选人均曾在不同时期服务于工部局各委员会，且在過去一年中均以某种程度参与了工部局的活动。

当新一届市政领导人在纳税人年会后就职时，议事厅中将见不到两位熟悉的身影。卸任工部局主席、多年来在市政事务中颇具影响力的 E. B. Macnaghten 先生此次不作为候选人，因为他将前往英国长期休假。

出于同样原因，现任工部局董事 E. F. Harris 先生也不作为候选人。

Arnhold 先生（主席）、J. W. Carney、C. S. Franklin、W. P. Lambe、J. H. Liddell 和 T. Yamamoto 均为现任工部局董事，他们将寻求连任。在这六人中，三人为英国人，两人为美国人，一人为日本人。

新面孔包括英国社区的三位成员：Porter 先生、Killery 先生和 Hughes 先生；Hossenlopp 先生为法国人；Urabe 先生为日本社区成员。

现任工部局的代表比例为五名英国董事、两名美国董事和两名日本董事。随着一名法国候选人和一名额外英国候选人的加入，人们以极大的兴趣等待即将举行的选举结果。

**商界人士**

A. J. Hughes 先生实际上并非工部局事务的新人，他此前曾担任董事，随后又在工部局各委员会任职。他是中华联合保险公司（China United Assurance Society, Ltd.）的经理。

L. R. Hossenlopp 先生此前未参与租界的市政事务，但一直是工部局乐队与管弦乐委员会的成员。他是本市知名的马塞尔（Marcel）企业的业主。

V. St. J. Killery 先生对于地方市政管理而言也相对较新，但在过去一年中一直是工部局交通委员会的成员。他是帝国化学工业有限公司（Imperial Chemical Industries, Ltd.）的董事总经理。

Harold Porter 爵士（C.M.G.）首次参选董事，但在过去一年中一直是工部局捐税估价委员会的成员。他是本地知名的商人，多年来与福公司（Pekin Syndicate）有关联。

T. Urabe 先生除了是工务委员会委员外，此前并未参与地方市政事务。他是三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）的经理。

在提名公布前的一段时间里，坊间广泛传言日本社区将在工部局寻求增加一名代表，尽管对于是否应在下次选举中提出此问题意见不一，但在昨天中午提名揭晓之前，关于日本候选人数目仍存在一些疑问。最终只有两名候选人代表日本社区。

**土地委员会**

H. G. F. Robinson 先生由 N. L. Sparke 先生提名，A. W. Burkill 先生附议，根据《土地章程》第六条甲款，被视为当选为1935市政年度的土地委员。
